title: Pentecostarion: Pascha to the Monday of the Holy Spirit
scope: One entry for every day from Pascha (pascha 0) to the Monday of the Holy Spirit (pascha 50), keyed by days after Pascha.
licence: Released with bible-rs under the MIT licence. The table holds Scripture references only: no Bible text and no prose from the sources. Notes are our own.
usage: Antiochian Orthodox Christian Archdiocese of North America: Byzantine (Greek) usage, Revised Julian fixed feasts, Julian Paschalion. Slavic (OCA) and Greek (GOARCH) differences are kept in 'variants' and 'slavic' and never replace the main reading.
numbering: English Bible (KJV/Hebrew) chapter and verse, the grid's numbering, with half-verse letters dropped. Each string in refs is one contiguous range ('Book C:V', 'Book C:V-V' or 'Book C:V-C:V', with the grid's book abbreviations); a reading's refs are read together, in order, as one lesson.
confidence: high: an Antiochian-facing source agrees with at least one independent source. medium: the sources differ (usually by a verse at the start or end) or the reference rests on one source. low: no Antiochian or Greek source was found, or the yearly ordo decides.

sources.ANT-OLG: Antiochian Archdiocese, Department of Liturgics: Online Liturgical Guide service texts, 2023-2026 (antiochian.org/servicetexts). References only.
sources.ANT-CHART: Antiochian Archdiocese, Sunday Liturgical Readings Chart 2026 (antiochian.org/liturgicalinstructions).
sources.ANT: antiochian.org daily readings, 2018-2026 (the GOARCH Online Chapel feed, as harvested in orthocal-python's data/antiochian_raw).
sources.GOA: Greek Orthodox Archdiocese of America, Online Chapel daily readings, 2018-2030 (goarch.org; partly as harvested in orthocal-python).
sources.GOA-DCS: GOA Digital Chant Stand (dcs.goarch.org), 'Readings for the Day', 2026.
sources.OCA: Orthodox Church in America lectionary, via the orthocal.info API, 2010-2032. Slavic usage.
sources.HAP: Isabel F. Hapgood, Service Book of the Holy Orthodox-Catholic Apostolic (Greco-Russian) Church, 1906 (public domain; archive.org cu31924029363128): tables of Epistles and Gospels.
sources.SCR: F. H. Scrivener, A Plain Introduction to the Criticism of the New Testament, Cambridge 1861 (public domain; archive.org plainintroductio00scri): Synaxarion and Menologion of the Byzantine lectionary manuscripts.
sources.GRE: V. Grechulevich, Ukazatel tserkovnykh chtenii, St Petersburg 1853 (public domain): Slavic lectionary index with zachalo numbers.
sources.MCI: Metropolitan Cantor Institute (Byzantine Catholic Archeparchy of Pittsburgh), 'The Lectionary' (mci.archpitt.org). Slavic usage.
sources.NLM: New Liturgical Movement: descriptions of the Antiochian Paschal procession (2019) and the Royal Hours of Theophany (2017).
sources.WIKI: Wikipedia, articles on the Triodion and Holy Week (for Holy Week Old Testament readings only).

rules: Acts is the Epistle and John the Gospel every day, except Bright Tuesday, Myrrhbearers Sunday, the Ascension and the Monday of the Holy Spirit. Nothing shifts in this season.
Vespers readings marked 'evening before' are sung on the eve. The Agape Vespers Gospel is filed under Pascha.
Sunday Matins Gospels follow the Antiochian chart (eothina 1, 4, 5, 7, 8, 10).
Fixed feasts that meet this season (St George, the Apostle John, Sts Constantine and Helen) are in menaion.json.

entries.name: Holy Pascha (Sunday of the Resurrection)

readings.served: at the start of Paschal Matins, read outside the closed church doors
afternoon or evening of Pascha (Agape Vespers)

entries.note: Liturgy and Agape Vespers readings are high confidence. The Matins Gospel Mark 16:1-8 is Byzantine/Greek usage, read at the doors before the first 'Christ is risen'. It rests on the GOARCH feed and a description of Antiochian practice, not an Antiochian rubric text (medium). Antiochian rubric: the Agape Vespers Gospel is read in as many languages as possible. orthocal files the Agape Vespers Gospel under Bright Monday, because liturgically it is that day's Vespers. Slavic usage (Hapgood 1906, orthocal) has no Matins Gospel at Pascha.

entries.name: Bright Monday
entries.note: Greek and Antiochian practice: when St George (23 April) falls before Pascha, his feast moves to Bright Monday and his readings are added or substituted. This is a menaion interaction, not part of this table. Slavic parishes may also hold a Paschal cross procession with five Gospels (Matt 28:1-20, Mark 16:1-8, Luke 24:1-12, John 20:1-10, Luke 24:36-53). That is not Antiochian usage.

entries.name: Bright Tuesday
Bright Wednesday
entries.note: The Epistle's end verse is disputed. GOARCH (and so antiochian.org) reads Acts 2:22-38. Scrivener's manuscripts, OCA, the Metropolitan Cantor Institute and akroasis read Acts 2:22-36. No independent printed Greek or Antiochian Apostolos was available to settle it. The Gospel is certain. Scrivener prints John 1:35-52, which reflects a different verse division; English Bibles end the chapter at 1:51. Scrivener's manuscript table also orders this week's Acts lessons differently (Wed 2:38-43, Thu 3:1-8, Fri 2:22-36). No modern source follows that order.

entries.name: Mid-Pentecost (Wednesday of the 4th Week)
entries.note: The Vespers readings are composites. Mic 5:4-5 uses English (KJV) numbering; it is Mic 5:3-4 in Hebrew Bibles. Only 5:4 is actually read. The Antiochian rubric heads the Isaiah lesson '55:1-2; 12:3-4; 55:2-3, 6-13'; the refs here follow the text as read, which leaves out 55:4-5. OCA lists Isa 55:1; 12:3-4; 55:2-13. There is no Matins Gospel. Slavic usage adds a small blessing of waters (Heb 2:11-18; John 5:1-4 per orthocal). It is not Antiochian usage.

Friday of the 7th Week (Leave-taking of the Ascension)
Saturday of Souls (Saturday before Pentecost)
entries.note: Usages differ on this day. Antiochian service texts read the day's Acts and John only, with the prokeimenon and hymns of the departed. GOARCH and its feed (shown on antiochian.org) put the Epistle of the departed in place of Acts. Slavic usage reads both the day's pair and the pair for the departed. No Matins Gospel; the Friday-evening Vespers has no readings.

entries.name: Holy Pentecost (Sunday of the Holy Trinity)
entries.note: Joel 2:23-32 uses English (KJV) numbering; in Hebrew Bibles it is Joel 2:23-27 and 3:1-5. The Gospel skips John 7:53-8:11, as every source does. Hapgood's Great Feasts table misprints the Pentecost Gospel as 'Luke xvi. 15-18; xvii. 1-4'; its own Sunday table gives John 7:37-52, 8:12. The Kneeling Vespers on Pentecost evening has no readings; it is liturgically the Vespers of Monday.

entries.name: Monday of the Holy Spirit
entries.note: Hapgood prints Eph 5:9-19. The Slavic pericope begins mid-way through 5:8, and with the half-verse letter dropped that is 5:8.
